Motorcycle Hand Signals Every Rider Should Know

Clear communication saves lives in group riding. These 10 signals are universally understood by UK riders. Read our Best Motorcycle Roads in Scotland: 15 Must-Ride Routes guide for more. Read our UK Road Hazards Every Biker Must Know guide for more. Read our Motorcycle Helmet Safety Ratings Explained guide for more.

  1. Left Turn — Left arm extended straight.
  2. Right Turn — Left arm bent upward at 90 degrees.
  3. Stop — Left arm extended down, palm facing back.
  4. Slow Down — Left arm extended, palm down, waving down.
  5. Speed Up — Left arm extended, palm up, waving up.
  6. Follow Me — Left arm raised, palm forward, waving.
  7. Hazard Right — Right foot pointed out.
  8. Hazard Left — Left hand pointing down to the left.
  9. Single File — Left index finger raised above helmet.
  10. Fuel Stop — Left arm out, pointing to tank.
Always agree signals with your group before setting off.
keyTakeaways: Ten universal hand signals keep group rides safe and coordinated.
Most turn and speed signals use the left arm to keep the right hand on the throttle.
Hazard signals use a pointed foot or hand to warn of road debris on either side.
The single-file signal is a left index finger raised above the helmet.
Always agree your group's signals before setting off to avoid confusion.

faq.q: Why do motorcyclists use hand signals?
faq.a: Hand signals let riders communicate clearly in group rides where intercoms may not reach everyone. They warn of turns, stops, hazards and formation changes, keeping the group coordinated and safe. Because most bikes lack a passenger to relay messages, a shared set of signals is the reliable way to pass information down the line.

faq.q: Why are most signals given with the left hand?
faq.a: The right hand controls the throttle and front brake, so keeping it on the bars maintains control while signalling. The left hand operates the clutch, which can be released briefly to give a signal. Foot signals are used for hazards on the right so the rider does not have to remove the throttle hand.

faq.q: How do you signal a road hazard to the group?
faq.a: Point your left hand down to the left to indicate a hazard on the left side of the road, and point your right foot out to indicate a hazard on the right, keeping your throttle hand on the bars. These signals warn following riders of potholes, gravel, debris or other dangers so they can position safely.

Raising your left index finger above your helmet tells the group to move into single file, usually because the road is narrowing, traffic is approaching, or conditions require more spacing. The opposite formation and other changes should be agreed beforehand so everyone reacts the same way when the signal is given.

faq.q: Should a group agree signals before riding?
faq.a: Yes, always. While many signals are near-universal, riders come from different backgrounds and some gestures vary, so a quick briefing before setting off prevents dangerous misunderstandings. Agree the signals for turns, stops, hazards, fuel stops and formation changes, and confirm the running order and lead and sweep riders.
